newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling strengthens against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling strengthens against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling strengthened against the dollar on Thursday to below 55 reflecting a calm and stable market, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.95 against the dollar from 55.22. Against the pound it was posted at a mean rate of 90.30 from 89.76.
"The market is stable and matched. Rates are trading stuck at 54.75/55.00," a dealer said.
Dealers in the market said the shilling's return below 55 was expected as the shilling's weakening above that level on Monday was driven by panic buying and speculation which had diminished.
"The hike in the dollar's value was artificial and overstated," another dealer said.
They said they expected the shilling to strengthen for the rest of the week in an active interbank market, trading at thin margins.
The money market remained liquid with rates quoted between five and 10 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
